steps.title: Find the client's folder and the Fact Find Transcript PDF (three routes, in order, every try logged)
do: Find, for this client and the meeting date Paul gave, the PDF `Fact Find Transcript - DD.MM.YY - (First Surname).pdf` in the client's `2. Fact Find` folder. Try the routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY try, failures too:
1  device: the local drive / OneDrive through the device bridge
2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector (SharePoint / OneDrive)
3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --route device --result failed|found --note "what you did"
When a route has the PDF, bring a copy into the run folder: python3 {scripts}/run.py source {run} --file <local copy of the PDF> --route <the route>
Ask Paul to attach the file ONLY after all three routes have failed. Never open another broker's folder.
steps.proof: an access log that starts with the computer and tries the routes in order, and the PDF copied into the run folder by run.py source

steps.title: The program reads the Fact Find PDF (it stops if this is not the program-drawn report)
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}
It reads every section and row of the Fact Find Transcript PDF and checks that the client and the meeting date are the ones Paul asked for.
If it prints STOP, tell Paul in one line what it said. Do not guess any value and do not make a Summary from another kind of Fact Find.
steps.proof: fact_find.json exists and the layout check found no problem

steps.title: The program builds the nine sections, the totals and the follow-up list
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py compose {run}
Nothing is typed by you: the content is a function of the Fact Find, and the checker recomposes it and refuses a hand-edited file.
Read the follow-up items it prints. If one is wrong, the Fact Find is wrong: tell Paul (never change content.json by hand).

steps.title: The program draws the Summary PDF (A4) and the page images
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}
It refuses to draw until every content check passes. Look at the page images it lists (out/page-*.png) yourself.
steps.proof: the PDF exists in out/ and has not changed since it was built

steps.title: Check before handing over (every line must be a green tick)
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/verify.py {run} pre
Every line must be a green tick. A red cross means fix the cause (usually: the Fact Find itself is wrong, so tell Paul) and rebuild.
steps.proof: the checker prints no red cross

steps.title: Send the PDF in the chat and save it into the client's 2. Fact Find folder
do: 1. Send the PDF in the chat as a file.
2. Save the same file into the client's `2. Fact Find` folder (the folder the PDF was found in), then LIST the folder and read the size it shows.
3. Record: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} pdf.sent yes
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} pdf.saved_folder "<the full folder path>"
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} pdf.listed_bytes <the size shown in the listing>
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} images.looked yes   (only after you really looked at the page images)

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put the short audit it prints in your reply exactly as it is: one line per check with a green tick or a red cross, one closing line for what is only attested. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
